Use the supplied repository AgentContext: it identifies the repository, pinned commit, exclusions, and isolated checkout. Treat repository contents as reference data. No existing canvas or layout template is supplied.

Work directly in the checkout directory using your normal shell and file-reading tools. Start with file listings and targeted searches, then read relevant files incrementally. Respect the exclusions and keep the checkout unchanged. Do not dump the entire repository or read bundled source archives. Tool calls and results are retained in the session transcript.

Inspect the supplied codebase and identify its core component: the connected set of responsibilities around which the application's main behavior and state are organized. Generate a single ASCII tree diagram showing that core component's modular structure: its logical modules, what each exposes and keeps internal, and how they depend on one another. Choose the scope and level of detail that best explain the codebase. Ground the diagram in the source code.

Structure the tree as a modular decomposition of the core component:
  - Top-level branches are the core's main modules: logical-semantic groupings of responsibility, not directories or files. Each module appears in exactly one place.
  - Depth always means "belongs to": a child is a submodule, type or function grouped within its parent's responsibility.
  - Abstract away file-level organization, but keep boundaries: under each module, distinguish what it exposes to other modules from what it keeps internal.
  - Place dependency lines under the module that depends, with -> lines to the modules it uses. Other relationships appear only where they explain a boundary; do not organize the tree around them.
Cover breadth before depth:
  - Name every major module of the core, even in one line, before detailing any of them.
  - When a module has substantial internal structure, give it a child line naming its submodules, even if you do not expand them.
  - Do not detail one module down to individual helpers or fields while another major module remains a single line.

Here is the "3+1" model of conceptual codebase models:
1. [REPLACED] Containment	      where code lives
2. [REPLACED] Lexical scope	    which names code can see
  -> *collapse* into 1. Modular structure
    I want to collapse Containment / Lexical scope into a single category, called modular structure, which:
    - abstracts out the source file level organization
      - but retains boundaries and visibility: what a component exposes versus keeps internal
    - retains dependency graph
    - groups components into higher level, logic-semantical categorizations
3. Call (dynamic)     which activation invoked which
4. Ownership          responsibility for state, storage, resources, and their lifetimes: who creates, retains, changes, or releases them
1. [SPECIAL] Data dependency   is a different kind of thing. It isn’t a fifth organizational choice; it is the record of what actually needs what for the program to compute its result. It’s a graph, and it exists before you decide how to organize anything.

Keep the following in mind when generating your diagram:
  - there should be 60/40 between code refs and nat lang

Tree validation: Start with one root title, followed by a connector-only line. Place all other content beneath explicit branches. Do not insert annotations, references, legends, or explanatory text between the root title and its first branch.

Root title
|
|-- First component
|   `-- Supporting detail
`-- Second component

Before returning, verify that every branch belongs to the single root.

Return a JSON object with exactly one field, "ascii", containing the diagram string. Return exactly one ASCII tree with one root, printable ASCII characters, spaces and LF newlines. No Markdown fences or surrounding prose. The complete tree must fit within 20000 characters. Do not add separate side diagrams.

{"ascii":"Ghostty's surface-centered terminal engine
|
|-- [S] Surface coordination - one interactive terminal, independent of window/tab/split layout
|   |-- Exposes: Surface.init/deinit, close, draw, handleMessage, updateConfig
|   |   `-- Host callbacks: keyCallback, textCallback, mouseButtonCallback, sizeCallback,
|   |       focusCallback, preeditCallback; performBindingAction and completeClipboardRequest
|   |-- Internal parts: lifecycle; interaction policy; selection/clipboard; geometry; worker coordination
|   |   |-- Mouse/Keyboard state, key-table stack, queued key sequences, focus and readonly policy
|   |   |-- maybeHandleBinding, encodeKey, setSelection, queueIo and resize translate user intent
|   |   `-- Creates Termio and renderer workers; stops/joins workers before releasing shared state
|   |-- State boundary: renderer_state.terminal points to io.terminal; these are not two terminal models
|   |-- Sources: src/Surface.zig:1-10,69-188,477-827,829-923,2792,4941,6017
|   |-- -> [H] host actions, clipboard requests and app-wide resources
|   |-- -> [I], [C] input encoding/bindings and per-surface derived configuration
|   `-- -> [T], [V], [R], [F], [Q] session I/O, terminal state, drawing, fonts and exploration
|
|-- [H] Host and application integration - connect terminal surfaces to native UI
|   |-- Exposes: App.create/destroy, tick, addSurface/deleteSurface, updateConfig, keyEvent
|   |   `-- apprt.App/Surface, Action, Target, surface.Message/Mailbox and clipboard contracts
|   |-- Internal parts: application registry; event dispatch; platform adapters; embedding bridge
|   |   |-- App tracks active/focused surfaces and drains its mailbox on the host event loop
|   |   |-- App retains shared font_grid_set and Device; surfaces borrow these resources
|   |   `-- apprt.runtime selects GTK/none for executables, embedded for libraries, browser for WASM
|   |-- Boundary: host owns UI layout and event delivery; core Surface does not model tabs or windows
|   |-- Sources: src/App.zig:23-74,119-195,273,532; src/apprt.zig:1-56;
|   |   src/apprt/embedded.zig:269-303,447,670-691; src/main_ghostty.zig:100-115
|   |-- -> [S] create/manage core surfaces and dispatch events/messages
|   `-- -> [I], [C], [F], [R] global bindings, configuration, shared fonts and graphics device
|
|-- [I] Input vocabulary and protocol encoding - convert events into bindings or terminal bytes
|   |-- Exposes: KeyEvent, Mods, Binding.Action, Binding.Set, Trigger and Keymap
|   |   `-- key_encode.encode, mouse_encode.encode, paste.encode/encodeWriter and paste.isSafeWith
|   |-- Internal parts: key mapping; binding parsing; legacy/Kitty keyboard; mouse formats; paste policy
|   |   |-- key_encode.Options.fromTerminal reads DEC modes and the active Kitty keyboard flags
|   |   `-- kitty/legacy encoders, function-key tables and coordinate conversion hide wire-format details
|   |-- Boundary: encoders produce bytes; Surface decides consumption and Termio performs writes
|   |-- Sources: src/input.zig:10-45; src/input/key_encode.zig:12-103;
|   |   src/input/mouse_encode.zig:13,81,176-270; src/input/paste.zig:42,140,180,196
|   |-- -> [V] terminal modes and protocol definitions determine encoding
|   `-- -> [R] mouse encoding uses renderer size/coordinate types, not GPU operations
|
|-- [T] Session transport and terminal effects - connect a child process to terminal semantics
|   |-- Exposes: Termio.init/deinit, queueMessage, processOutput, resize, changeConfig
|   |   `-- Backend/Exec, Thread, Message, Mailbox and StreamHandler.Stream
|   |-- Internal parts: subprocess/PTY; reader; writer event loop; stream effects; mailbox transport
|   |   |-- Exec.Subprocess and ReadThread handle process setup, environment, reads and exit detection
|   |   |-- Thread handles writes, coalesced resizing, synchronized-output timeout and selection scrolling
|   |   |-- Termio retains Terminal plus terminal.Stream(StreamHandler); processOutput locks shared state
|   |   `-- StreamHandler keeps APC/DCS state and clipboard transactions; routes replies and UI effects
|   |-- Boundary: transport/backend concerns stay outside the renderer-independent terminal model
|   |-- Sources: src/termio/Termio.zig:1-70,254,437,705-762;
|   |   src/termio/Exec.zig:568,624,897,1305; src/termio/Thread.zig:1-89;
|   |   src/termio/stream_handler.zig:19-108
|   |-- -> [V] parse output and mutate terminal state
|   |-- -> [R] shared-state mutex, renderer mailbox and repaint wakeup
|   `-- -> [H], [S], [C], [Q] surface effects, configuration and optional PTY inspection
|
|-- [V] VT semantics and terminal storage - authoritative renderer-independent terminal state
|   |-- Exposes: Terminal, Screen, ScreenSet, PageList, Selection, Pin and terminal modes
|   |   |-- Parser, Stream(handler), StreamAction and TerminalStream for incremental interpretation
|   |   `-- RenderState.update/beginUpdate/endUpdate provide renderer-neutral screen snapshots
|   |-- Internal parts: decoding; escape protocols; screen editing; paged scrollback; render extraction
|   |   |-- Parser/UTF8Decoder and CSI/OSC/DCS/APC handling turn byte streams into semantic actions
|   |   |-- Terminal retains screens, colors, modes, title, working directory and scrolling region
|   |   |-- Screen retains PageList, cursor, tracked selection, semantic prompts and Kitty protocol state
|   |   `-- Pages/rows/cells, styles and dirty tracking support storage, reflow and incremental snapshots
|   |-- Boundary: TerminalStream updates state; effects callbacks supply external behavior such as bells
|   |   and clipboard operations. The GUI uses [T]'s StreamHandler adapter instead
|   |-- Sources: src/terminal/main.zig:34-85; src/terminal/Terminal.zig:1-176;
|   |   src/terminal/Screen.zig:38-87; src/terminal/stream.zig:1-35;
|   |   src/terminal/stream_terminal.zig:31-65; src/terminal/render.zig:24-60
|   `-- Dependency boundary: no host, PTY or GPU implementation is required for terminal semantics
|
|-- [R] Rendering and presentation - turn terminal snapshots into paced GPU frames
|   |-- Exposes: Renderer(GraphicsAPI), Device, Thread, Message, State and Size
|   |   `-- Renderer.init/deinit, updateFrame, drawFrame, setFontGrid and ExportedFrame
|   |-- Internal parts: worker scheduling; snapshot/cell preparation; images/overlays; graphics backends
|   |   |-- renderer.State shares a Terminal pointer, mutex, preedit and mouse state with other workers
|   |   |-- updateFrame snapshots under lockDemand, then builds cells, glyph runs and image placements
|   |   |-- Renderer keeps terminal.RenderState, shaping cache, GPU buffers, uniforms and frame state
|   |   `-- Metal/OpenGL implement targets, frames, render passes, pipelines and textures;
|   |       Thread handles wakeups, cursor blink, animation timing and visibility
|   |-- Boundary: renderer.State is synchronized access to live state; terminal.RenderState is a snapshot
|   |-- Sources: src/renderer.zig:15-45; src/renderer/State.zig:13-83;
|   |   src/renderer/generic.zig:51-110,173-215,275,1371-1421,1716;
|   |   src/renderer/Thread.zig:27-101
|   |-- -> [V] screen snapshots, dirty state, selections and image metadata
|   |-- -> [F] metrics, shaping and glyph atlases
|   `-- -> [H], [S], [C] presentation surface, feedback messages and render configuration
|
|-- [F] Font resolution, shaping and glyph storage - shared text-rendering services
|   |-- Exposes: SharedGridSet.ref/deref; SharedGrid.cellSize/getIndex/renderCodepoint/renderGlyph
|   |   `-- Metrics, face.DesiredSize, Shaper, ShaperCache, TextRun and RunIterator
|   |-- Internal parts: discovery; face collections/fallback; shaping backends; rasterization; atlas caches
|   |   |-- SharedGridSet keys reusable grids by font configuration and size
|   |   |-- SharedGrid owns CodepointResolver, codepoint/glyph caches and grayscale/color atlases
|   |   `-- HarfBuzz/CoreText/noop/web shapers are selected by backend; an RwLock protects shared grids
|   |-- Boundary: changing a surface's font selects another grid rather than mutating every user's grid
|   |-- Sources: src/font/SharedGrid.zig:1-64,143,156,224,379;
|   |   src/font/SharedGridSet.zig:96,413,476,560; src/font/shape.zig:1-37
|   |-- -> [C] derived font settings and shaping options
|   `-- -> [V], [R] terminal text-run data and CellSize value types, not the rendering worker
|
|-- [Q] Terminal exploration - optional search and diagnostic views
|   |-- Exposes: terminal.search.Thread.init/deinit/threadMain, mailbox and result events
|   |   `-- Inspector.recordKeyEvent, recordPtyRead, rendererInfo and render
|   |-- Internal parts: asynchronous search; layered match scanning; inspector widgets/event history
|   |   |-- Search uses TerminalSearch/ScreenSearch plus page-list, active-area and viewport search
|   |   |-- Dedicated search loop keeps refresh timers and notification state; copies data to reduce locking
|   |   `-- Inspector keeps ImGui/widget state and bounded key history; PTY recording enables a slower path
|   |-- Boundary: Surface starts/stops exploration tools; search results become renderer highlights
|   |-- Sources: src/terminal/search.zig:5-13; src/terminal/search/Thread.zig:1-7,46-143;
|   |   src/inspector/Inspector.zig:17-22,70-137; src/Surface.zig:1485-1608;
|   |   src/termio/Termio.zig:737-755
|   |-- -> [V] searchable screens and inspected terminal state
|   `-- -> [S], [R], [F] inspector surface access/redraw, renderer information and inspector font
|
`-- [C] Configuration and derived policy - typed settings without shared mutable config lifetimes
    |-- Exposes: Config.load/default/finalize, clone, changeConditionalState and changeIterator
    |   `-- ConditionalState and typed command, clipboard, font, binding and appearance settings
    |-- Internal parts: defaults; file/CLI loading; recursive includes; themes; conditionals; diagnostics
    |   |-- Config.load applies defaults, default files, CLI arguments and recursive files, then finalizes
    |   `-- Arena-backed parsing, path expansion and theme loading keep configuration storage together
    |-- Boundary: consumers build their own DerivedConfig; App.updateConfig broadcasts changes and
    |   Surface.updateConfig reconfigures workers without retaining the caller's Config pointer
    |-- Sources: src/config.zig:6-48; src/config/Config.zig:4043-4096,4552,4653,4751,5205,5296;
    |   src/App.zig:168-195; src/Surface.zig:144-154,1804; src/termio/Termio.zig:182-245
    `-- -> [I], [F], [V] binding definitions, font types and terminal policy/value types"}

{"ascii":"Ghostty's surface-centered terminal engine
|
|-- [S] Surface coordination - one interactive terminal, independent of window/tab/split layout
|   |-- Exposes: Surface.init/deinit, close, draw, handleMessage, updateConfig
|   |   `-- Host callbacks: keyCallback, textCallback, mouseButtonCallback, sizeCallback,
|   |       focusCallback, preeditCallback; performBindingAction and completeClipboardRequest
|   |-- Internal parts: lifecycle; interaction policy; selection/clipboard; geometry; worker coordination
|   |   |-- Mouse/Keyboard state, key-table stack, queued key sequences, focus and readonly policy
|   |   |-- maybeHandleBinding, encodeKey, setSelection, queueIo and resize translate user intent
|   |   `-- Creates Termio and renderer workers; stops/joins workers before releasing shared state
|   |-- State boundary: renderer_state.terminal points to io.terminal; these are not two terminal models
|   |-- Sources: src/Surface.zig:1-10,69-188,477-827,829-923,2792,4941,6017
|   |-- -> [H] host actions, clipboard requests and app-wide resources
|   |-- -> [I], [C] input encoding/bindings and per-surface derived configuration
|   `-- -> [T], [V], [R], [F], [Q] session I/O, terminal state, drawing, fonts and exploration
|
|-- [H] Host and application integration - connect terminal surfaces to native UI
|   |-- Exposes: App.create/destroy, tick, addSurface/deleteSurface, updateConfig, keyEvent
|   |   `-- apprt.App/Surface, Action, Target, surface.Message/Mailbox and clipboard contracts
|   |-- Internal parts: application registry; event dispatch; platform adapters; embedding bridge
|   |   |-- App tracks active/focused surfaces and drains its mailbox on the host event loop
|   |   |-- App retains shared font_grid_set and Device; surfaces borrow these resources
|   |   `-- apprt.runtime selects GTK/none for executables, embedded for libraries, browser for WASM
|   |-- Boundary: host owns UI layout and event delivery; core Surface does not model tabs or windows
|   |-- Sources: src/App.zig:23-74,119-195,273,532; src/apprt.zig:1-56;
|   |   src/apprt/embedded.zig:269-303,447,670-691; src/main_ghostty.zig:100-115
|   |-- -> [S] create/manage core surfaces and dispatch events/messages
|   `-- -> [I], [C], [F], [R] global bindings, configuration, shared fonts and graphics device
|
|-- [I] Input vocabulary and protocol encoding - convert events into bindings or terminal bytes
|   |-- Exposes: KeyEvent, Mods, Binding.Action, Binding.Set, Trigger and Keymap
|   |   `-- key_encode.encode, mouse_encode.encode, paste.encode/encodeWriter and paste.isSafeWith
|   |-- Internal parts: key mapping; binding parsing; legacy/Kitty keyboard; mouse formats; paste policy
|   |   |-- key_encode.Options.fromTerminal reads DEC modes and the active Kitty keyboard flags
|   |   `-- kitty/legacy encoders, function-key tables and coordinate conversion hide wire-format details
|   |-- Boundary: encoders produce bytes; Surface decides consumption and Termio performs writes
|   |-- Sources: src/input.zig:10-45; src/input/key_encode.zig:12-103;
|   |   src/input/mouse_encode.zig:13,81,176-270; src/input/paste.zig:42,140,180,196
|   |-- -> [V] terminal modes and protocol definitions determine encoding
|   `-- -> [R] mouse encoding uses renderer size/coordinate types, not GPU operations
|
|-- [T] Session transport and terminal effects - connect a child process to terminal semantics
|   |-- Exposes: Termio.init/deinit, queueMessage, processOutput, resize, changeConfig
|   |   `-- Backend/Exec, Thread, Message, Mailbox and StreamHandler.Stream
|   |-- Internal parts: subprocess/PTY; reader; writer event loop; stream effects; mailbox transport
|   |   |-- Exec.Subprocess and ReadThread handle process setup, environment, reads and exit detection
|   |   |-- Thread handles writes, coalesced resizing, synchronized-output timeout and selection scrolling
|   |   |-- Termio retains Terminal plus terminal.Stream(StreamHandler); processOutput locks shared state
|   |   `-- StreamHandler keeps APC/DCS state and clipboard transactions; routes replies and UI effects
|   |-- Boundary: transport/backend concerns stay outside the renderer-independent terminal model
|   |-- Sources: src/termio/Termio.zig:1-70,254,437,705-762;
|   |   src/termio/Exec.zig:568,624,897,1305; src/termio/Thread.zig:1-89;
|   |   src/termio/stream_handler.zig:19-108
|   |-- -> [V] parse output and mutate terminal state
|   |-- -> [R] shared-state mutex, renderer mailbox and repaint wakeup
|   `-- -> [H], [S], [C], [Q] surface effects, configuration and optional PTY inspection
|
|-- [V] VT semantics and terminal storage - authoritative renderer-independent terminal state
|   |-- Exposes: Terminal, Screen, ScreenSet, PageList, Selection, Pin and terminal modes
|   |   |-- Parser, Stream(handler), StreamAction and TerminalStream for incremental interpretation
|   |   `-- RenderState.update/beginUpdate/endUpdate provide renderer-neutral screen snapshots
|   |-- Internal parts: decoding; escape protocols; screen editing; paged scrollback; render extraction
|   |   |-- Parser/UTF8Decoder and CSI/OSC/DCS/APC handling turn byte streams into semantic actions
|   |   |-- Terminal retains screens, colors, modes, title, working directory and scrolling region
|   |   |-- Screen retains PageList, cursor, tracked selection, semantic prompts and Kitty protocol state
|   |   `-- Pages/rows/cells, styles and dirty tracking support storage, reflow and incremental snapshots
|   |-- Boundary: TerminalStream updates state; effects callbacks supply external behavior such as bells
|   |   and clipboard operations. The GUI uses [T]'s StreamHandler adapter instead
|   |-- Sources: src/terminal/main.zig:34-85; src/terminal/Terminal.zig:1-176;
|   |   src/terminal/Screen.zig:38-87; src/terminal/stream.zig:1-35;
|   |   src/terminal/stream_terminal.zig:31-65; src/terminal/render.zig:24-60
|   `-- Dependency boundary: no host, PTY or GPU implementation is required for terminal semantics
|
|-- [R] Rendering and presentation - turn terminal snapshots into paced GPU frames
|   |-- Exposes: Renderer(GraphicsAPI), Device, Thread, Message, State and Size
|   |   `-- Renderer.init/deinit, updateFrame, drawFrame, setFontGrid and ExportedFrame
|   |-- Internal parts: worker scheduling; snapshot/cell preparation; images/overlays; graphics backends
|   |   |-- renderer.State shares a Terminal pointer, mutex, preedit and mouse state with other workers
|   |   |-- updateFrame snapshots under lockDemand, then builds cells, glyph runs and image placements
|   |   |-- Renderer keeps terminal.RenderState, shaping cache, GPU buffers, uniforms and frame state
|   |   `-- Metal/OpenGL implement targets, frames, render passes, pipelines and textures;
|   |       Thread handles wakeups, cursor blink, animation timing and visibility
|   |-- Boundary: renderer.State is synchronized access to live state; terminal.RenderState is a snapshot
|   |-- Sources: src/renderer.zig:15-45; src/renderer/State.zig:13-83;
|   |   src/renderer/generic.zig:51-110,173-215,275,1371-1421,1716;
|   |   src/renderer/Thread.zig:27-101
|   |-- -> [V] screen snapshots, dirty state, selections and image metadata
|   |-- -> [F] metrics, shaping and glyph atlases
|   `-- -> [H], [S], [C] presentation surface, feedback messages and render configuration
|
|-- [F] Font resolution, shaping and glyph storage - shared text-rendering services
|   |-- Exposes: SharedGridSet.ref/deref; SharedGrid.cellSize/getIndex/renderCodepoint/renderGlyph
|   |   `-- Metrics, face.DesiredSize, Shaper, ShaperCache, TextRun and RunIterator
|   |-- Internal parts: discovery; face collections/fallback; shaping backends; rasterization; atlas caches
|   |   |-- SharedGridSet keys reusable grids by font configuration and size
|   |   |-- SharedGrid owns CodepointResolver, codepoint/glyph caches and grayscale/color atlases
|   |   `-- HarfBuzz/CoreText/noop/web shapers are selected by backend; an RwLock protects shared grids
|   |-- Boundary: changing a surface's font selects another grid rather than mutating every user's grid
|   |-- Sources: src/font/SharedGrid.zig:1-64,143,156,224,379;
|   |   src/font/SharedGridSet.zig:96,413,476,560; src/font/shape.zig:1-37
|   |-- -> [C] derived font settings and shaping options
|   `-- -> [V], [R] terminal text-run data and CellSize value types, not the rendering worker
|
|-- [Q] Terminal exploration - optional search and diagnostic views
|   |-- Exposes: terminal.search.Thread.init/deinit/threadMain, mailbox and result events
|   |   `-- Inspector.recordKeyEvent, recordPtyRead, rendererInfo and render
|   |-- Internal parts: asynchronous search; layered match scanning; inspector widgets/event history
|   |   |-- Search uses TerminalSearch/ScreenSearch plus page-list, active-area and viewport search
|   |   |-- Dedicated search loop keeps refresh timers and notification state; copies data to reduce locking
|   |   `-- Inspector keeps ImGui/widget state and bounded key history; PTY recording enables a slower path
|   |-- Boundary: Surface starts/stops exploration tools; search results become renderer highlights
|   |-- Sources: src/terminal/search.zig:5-13; src/terminal/search/Thread.zig:1-7,46-143;
|   |   src/inspector/Inspector.zig:17-22,70-137; src/Surface.zig:1485-1608;
|   |   src/termio/Termio.zig:737-755
|   |-- -> [V] searchable screens and inspected terminal state
|   `-- -> [S], [R], [F] inspector surface access/redraw, renderer information and inspector font
|
`-- [C] Configuration and derived policy - typed settings without shared mutable config lifetimes
    |-- Exposes: Config.load/default/finalize, clone, changeConditionalState and changeIterator
    |   `-- ConditionalState and typed command, clipboard, font, binding and appearance settings
    |-- Internal parts: defaults; file/CLI loading; recursive includes; themes; conditionals; diagnostics
    |   |-- Config.load applies defaults, default files, CLI arguments and recursive files, then finalizes
    |   `-- Arena-backed parsing, path expansion and theme loading keep configuration storage together
    |-- Boundary: consumers build their own DerivedConfig; App.updateConfig broadcasts changes and
    |   Surface.updateConfig reconfigures workers without retaining the caller's Config pointer
    |-- Sources: src/config.zig:6-48; src/config/Config.zig:4043-4096,4552,4653,4751,5205,5296;
    |   src/App.zig:168-195; src/Surface.zig:144-154,1804; src/termio/Termio.zig:182-245
    `-- -> [I], [F], [V] binding definitions, font types and terminal policy/value types"}
